newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT--Dollar correction may run out of steam.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT--Dollar correction may run out of steam.

text.p: After a week of solid gains, the dollar may be running out of steam and forced back to the bottom of its recent range, analysts said on Tuesday.
Dollar/yen and dollar/mark have rallied in tandem since setting recent lows on May 20 as the Federal Reserve decided to leave U.S. interest rates unchanged.
Dollar/yen surged from an intraday low of 111.88 on May 20 to an intraday high of 116.78 on Tuesday, while dollar/mark rose from 1.6745 to 1.7074 over the same timeframe.
On Tuesday, the dollar closed at 1.7045/55 marks versus 1.6975/85 at the open, and at 116.64/69 yen vs. 116.35/45.

"Dollar/mark broke through 1.70 today, above the levels made before the Fed's rate decision last week. We're closing constructively," said analyst Ben Morden at the advisory firm I.D.E.A. "But we are still in a topping pattern, an area where you want to get short."
Morden predicted the dollar/mark rally would "fade near 1.7120 -- a 62-percent retracement of the move from the high of 1.7389 on April 28 to the low of 1.6680 on May 12."
Morden also pointed out that 1.71 marks corresponded to the 40-day moving average for dollar/mark -- an average where a dollar rally stalled twice already in May.
Morden predicted that if the dollar/mark rally stalls at around 1.71, the ensuing pullback could extend to "1.68, maybe 1.6710, a two-month trendline."
The I.D.E.A. analyst had a brighter dollar/yen outlook, with "a big level at 117.00, the 220-day moving average."
"You could see a squeeze as high as 117.85, or the 38-percent retracement from the high (at 127.47) on May 1 to the low at 111.88 on May 12," Morden said.
Technicians cautioned a dollar/yen pullback may go all the way to 110.55 -- the November low from where the rally started and that may provide strong support through the summer months.

Chartists saw dollar/Swiss -- which closed at 1.4203/13 vs. 1.4162/67 at the open -- as toppish, with the upside capped in the 1.4310/60 area. They put near-term resistance at 1.4285 Swiss francs and support at 1.4100, then 1.4040.
On the European crosses, mark/Paris grabbed the spotlight after the stunning lead of the Left in the first round of the French general elections on Sunday.
Morden, who noted mark/Paris gapped up from 3.3705 to 3.3735, predicted that "if 3.3775 goes, we'll see a move to 3.3805." A mark/Paris rally usually weighs on dollar/mark.
